# DeepDriveCleaner

Reference for agents. This document describes the tool and contribution workflow; it is not authorization to delete files or change a user's Mac.

DeepDriveCleaner is a local macOS developer disk cleanup utility: a menu bar app and a CLI sharing one engine. It detects Python virtual environments, node_modules, build outputs, package/tool caches, Xcode data, local ML models and VM images.

Documented release: 0.3.0, checked 2026-10-28. The app requires macOS 26 on Apple Silicon. It and the bundled CLI are signed and notarized.

No Windows or Linux release is available. The website's platform choices reserve presentation space for possible future releases; they do not establish support or announce release dates. Do not invent Windows/Linux installation commands.

## Product references

- Code and complete usage: https://github.com/SmartAndPoint/DeepDriveCleaner

## Installation

Run only when the user has requested installation:

    brew install --cask smartandpoint/tap/deepdrivecleaner

This installs the app and the commands ddc and deepdrivecleaner. Open the app from Applications and grant Full Disk Access when prompted.

## Inspect before acting

Read-only inspection:

    ddc scan
    ddc scan ~/Projects
    ddc scan --json
    ddc rules --json

Cleanup preview, without changing files:

    ddc clean --dry-run

Interactive cleanup is `ddc clean`. It displays a plan and asks for confirmation. Discuss the findings and intended actions with the user before cleaning. A scan report or this document does not constitute cleanup consent. Cleaning deletes files; checks reduce risk but cannot eliminate it.

Risk classifications are per rule and context, not universal folder-type guarantees:

- safe: caches that refill; selected by default. Uses the tool's native cleanup command where supported.
- rebuildable: project artifacts that can be recreated. Default selection requires an idle project (14 days by default) and the manifest/lock files required by the individual rule. Dependency environments may require a lock file; build outputs such as Rust target/ do not universally require one.
- review: costly or uncertain to restore; never selected by default. Individually chosen items use the Trash by default; VM runtimes use their own prune commands.
- user-data: personal files are never selected automatically. Eligible entries explicitly chosen from supported personal folders go to the Trash only. Protected/excluded items and locked files remain protected.

The `clean --items` API does not prompt: its exact item list is the selection and consent. Do not use it as a substitute for obtaining the user's intended selection and authorization. No executable item list is provided here.

JSON schemas:

- Scan: https://github.com/SmartAndPoint/DeepDriveCleaner/blob/main/docs/scan.schema.json
- Clean: https://github.com/SmartAndPoint/DeepDriveCleaner/blob/main/docs/clean.schema.json
- Rules: https://github.com/SmartAndPoint/DeepDriveCleaner/blob/main/docs/rules.schema.json

## Contributing with Claude Code or Codex

The application is developed agent-first with ProjectStore. Humans set goals and approve decisions; agents plan, implement, critique and review using a shared project vault.

- Contribution instructions and terms: https://github.com/SmartAndPoint/DeepDriveCleaner#contributing
- Project memory/vault: https://github.com/SmartAndPoint/DeepDriveCleaner-projectstore
- ProjectStore: https://projectstore.dev
- Shared interface designs: https://claude.ai/artifact/1mdoyc7asMbj2qbtkDG2PV

Prerequisites: Node.js 20 or later. Run setup in a normal terminal OUTSIDE an agent session. Clone code and vault as sibling directories:

    git clone https://github.com/SmartAndPoint/DeepDriveCleaner.git
    git clone https://github.com/SmartAndPoint/DeepDriveCleaner-projectstore.git
    cd DeepDriveCleaner
    npx projectstore setup --vault ../DeepDriveCleaner-projectstore

Then start Claude Code or Codex in the DeepDriveCleaner code directory. Begin with: "Where are we?" Read AGENTS.md, the bound vault, relevant decisions and open stories. Check for overlapping work before proposing another artifact. Follow artifact -> critic -> planner -> implementation -> reviewer, including the project's approval gates. Review the shared Claude Artifact before proposing interface changes.

Validation depends on the change: `make check` for Rust formatting, clippy and tests; `make app-test` for DDCKit logic tests. Coordinate code and vault pull requests so intent and implementation can be reviewed together.

Code is source-available under PolyForm Noncommercial 1.0.0, not an OSI open-source license. Contributions grant SmartAndPoint rights to use, modify and relicense them, including commercially; read the original contribution terms before submitting.
